label: Formulated the foundational dyadic sign model (signifier/signified) and differential value in Course in General Linguistics
description: Ferdinand de Saussure formulated and introduced the concept of "Semiology & The Arbitrary Sign", which became a seminal contribution in epistemology philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in epistemology.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis as part of Ferdinand de Saussure's canonical writings.

label: Saussure's structuralism provided the epistemic framework for Foucault's analysis of discursive formations in The Order of Things
description: Michel Foucault was fundamentally influenced by Ferdinand de Saussure's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Ferdinand de Saussure's perspective to Michel Foucault's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis across history into the Contemporary & Post-Structural.

label: Derrida radicalized Saussure's thesis that in language there are only differences without positive terms into différance
description: Jacques Derrida adopted Ferdinand de Saussure's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Ferdinand de Saussure's perspective to Jacques Derrida's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis across history into the Contemporary & Post-Structural.
